text_fidelity_a: Omnia Oven. Your oven on the stove top. Ideal solution for boat oven, camp oven, and RV oven. Also known as a wonder pot. We are in our RV for much of the time, and did not want to use up our propane for cooking during the cold months.  The Omnia does not work on an induction stove, but works very well on a gas stove -- no surprise there.  I purchased an electric hot plate to use with the Omnia, and this combination works well.  I have baked muffins, cornbread, cakes, chicken casserole, cinnamon rolls, etc. and been quite pleased with the outcome. When I made a cake, iced it and sprinkled it with colored sprinkles, it looked like a giant donut.  I didn't hear anyone complaining, though!  Really, I couldn't be more pleased with this Omnia oven.  Food does not brown on the top as it would in a regular oven, but that may be because I use a hot plate as opposed to a gas fire -- don't know.  Would I purchase an Omnia again?  Absolutely!!  In fact, I have purchased this twice.  I made the mistake of placing a very hot Omnia on microfiber towels.  The synthetic towels melted to the bottom of the Omnia, and could not be removed. :(  So I learned the hard way to place a hot Omnia on  a silicone pad or 100% cotton toweling. I did purchase the 2-pack silicone liners which makes clean-up a breeze.  I also purchased the rack which keeps the bottom of food from over browning.  The oven and its bits and pieces all fit in the bag that comes with the Omnia, so when I grab the bag I have everything I need minus the hot plate.  The purchase of this Omnia is among the best purchases I made for our RV.
text_fidelity_b: Omnia Oven. Your oven on the stove top. Ideal solution for boat oven, camp oven, and RV oven. Also known as a wonder pot.

Joist Mount Pull Up Bar by Ultimate Body Press I had trepidation about purchasing such a joist-mounted pull-up bar, but decided it was the only real option I had for my basement gym. Assembly was difficult, but not from any fault of the product. Big question to ask yourself first:

Are you joists spaced far enough apart so that you can actually fit a drill w/ bit in between them to make the holes?

Turns out mine weren't, or rather, that almost all of them weren't, except for one awkwardly overspaced gap right up against a dividing wall that almost had enough to room to squeeze the drill in there and make holes. Anyway, after a few hours of cursing and intermittently giving up I finally got the thing up and it feels great. The handles are a good distance and offer many positions for hands to do chin/pull -ups. My joists are standard 2 in thick and about 10 in deep, I have the screws mounted about 4 inches up and so far it seems very sturdy. Hopefully nothing breaks, but thus far my expectations are high.
text_fidelity_b: Joist Mount Pull Up Bar by Ultimate Body Press

text_fidelity_a:
TOPOKO 25 OZ Hydro Double Wall Flask Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Bite Valve Top, Vacuum Insulated, Sweat Proof, Leak Proof Sports Thermos. Standard Mouth 25oz, BPA-Free, Keep Cold 24 Hours (Orange) As someone who like cold drinks and who lives in a warm climate, I realized my plastic bottles weren't keeping me happy. I had two stainless steel bottles around the house but one was designed for hot coffee and therefore a bit on the small size for someone who wants to fill it with a cold drink and a few cubes of ice. The other bottle was really similar to this only it had a twist off top and the top part was too small to squeeze standard ice cubes in. Took a chance on this one. The mouth is perfect for fitting ice cubes in. I went with the "bite" lid because I kind of get tired of opening and closing the bottle constantly and the straw lid seemed to get mixed reviews. The bite lid, so far, is perfect. I use it all day every day for my water. I have found the bite lid works best if you don't fully extend it, more like pull it up half way. When closed I shook it around and it didn't leak but I probably still wouldn't keep it in say a bag with anything important in it. I was using a slightly larger plastic bottle but find this bottle in this size is great as I don't need to cram as much ice in the bottle to keep it chilled.

I have seen some reviews that say the color coating peels off, I haven't had that experience thus far but I have heard of other bigger brand name bottles having the same issue when coated like this one is, so it wouldn't surprise me. Will update when / if I experience it.
text_fidelity_b: TOPOKO 25 OZ Hydro Double Wall Flask Stainless Steel Water Bottle, Bite Valve Top, Vacuum Insulated, Sweat Proof, Leak Proof Sports Thermos. Standard Mouth 25oz, BPA-Free, Keep Cold 24 Hours (Orange)

Outdoor Cooking Stove, Small Wood Stove. I have had a relationship with rocket stoves for about 20 years - the very first time I saw instructions on how to make a cheap/easy rocket stove from a paint can and large vegetable can with insulation material in between the two cans and then the next one I made was from concrete blocks.  Both were learning experiences and I fell in love with the idea of how they use very little fuel to create a decent fire.  This Light Me Bright rocket stove is not just a simple wood-burning one, but can be "changed out" to use charcoal briquettes as well.  Too cool!  But of course, the reason that I really love about this stove is that you can gather up some small twigs and pieces of wood - pinecones work too - and start a really impressive fire that cooks/boils water fast and easily.  Then, if you want to use charcoal instead, leave off the "rack" that holds wood, nearly close that front door and start your charcoal inside the stove.  Works well if you want a less "intense" fire, but however you use it, this is a nice sized, very portable rocket stove for camping or even for use outside (on my porch) during a power outage - you can still cook a meal if you have a tiny bit of wood or some charcoal.  This is one of the best stoves out there!

text_fidelity_a:
SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black There is a major difference between this tube and its non thorn-resistant counterparts. The difference translates to a 3x larger package and a 3x stiffer inner tube. Whether this means that it will intercede on your behalf when penetrating objects attempt to derail your day, time will tell. But I can tell you that:

1) It takes some effort to stuff this piece of salami into your tire. It doesn't bend willingly.
2) It takes some getting used to on the road. Your tire will absorb less shock from road imperfections, resulting in a harsh ride. It's not like riding on solid rubber, but it's not as soft as a regular inner tube.

In my opinion, the harsh ride is worth it on a daily commuter, where reliability is paramount. I'm not sure if I'd use this on a recreational bike. A suspension bike may be fine.

Update: after a week or two, I stopped noticing the stiffer ride quality. Also, I have about 50lbs extra on that rear wheel, so my experience may not be typical (it's an e-bike).
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Thorn Resistant Schrader Valve Tube, Black

FEND One Foldable Bike Helmet - Adult Mens and Womens Bike Helmet - Collapsible by 50% of Original Size - Safety Certified for Bicycle Road Bike Scooter Cycling Commuter Helmet… I've never been a regular wearer of helmets so I can't compare this to other brands, but this one suits me. The medium/large fits me well, and it's comfortable to wear throughout longer rides. It's also cooler than I expected, which is a real benefit as I live in a hot and often humid climate. And though it shouldn't matter, I like the simple design of this helmet as opposed to those that have a more aerodynamic look, so to speak. And I really appreciate the low-key logo; it's tasteful, not garish like you see on so many products.

But the most important thing for me is the fold. The main thing keeping me from wearing a helmet before was having to lump around a bowl. I know that's a bad reason, but it's the truth. This folds down enough to easily fit into all of my bike bags and even the small backpack that I often carry as a purse. Admittedly, it's a squeeze for the latter, and I don't carry much in that purse anyway, but the fact that it fits means that I'll use it, and using it is definitely safer than going without.

I was lucky to get a nice discount on this (for Prime Day, I think, though perhaps it was some other deal), but I think it's worth it at its regular price. Of course I hope never to give this the ultimate test, but it feels like a sound helmet and works for the way I bike. I'd definitely buy this again.
text_fidelity_b: FEND One Foldable Bike Helmet - Adult Mens and Womens Bike Helmet - Collapsible by 50% of Original Size - Safety Certified for Bicycle Road Bike Scooter Cycling Commuter Helmet…

Went back and forth with Hilboy for almost two weeks, sending videos of the problem and being told how they would make it right.
Then we get an email telling us that they need to physically see the item, it’s going to cost us $200 to “exchange” the item, and how they will only issue a refund of 50-60% depending on the problem. This doesn’t even include the cost to ship the item to them!
Incidentally, two days ago, their website said that they offered 12 months support and replacement/exchange on faulty bikes during that time frame. This has since been removed [I should have taken a screenshot shot of that, but I didn’t 🙄].
Finally, I called Amazon and told them what had been going on, and they’re going to take care of it.
So buyer beware. There are several reviews saying that this item doesn’t have a long life at all, and I can confirm this.
In addition, I can absolutely confirm that this manufacturer DOES NOT stand behind its product [as in my opinion, if it’s going to cost me anywhere near, or more than, what I paid for an item, for the manufacturer to even “consider” a replacement/exchange, then that is NO GUARANTEE].

BUY THIS PRODUCT AT YOUR OWN RISK!!!
YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!

Edit: got a FULL refund from Amazon and bought a similar one for less from a food warehouse store whose guarantee is “just bring it back if/when it ever breaks”

text_fidelity_a:
Desantis Nylon Ambidextrous Pocket Holster, Black I have carried a NAA five shot .22 magnum in my pocket ever since Florida allowed concealed weapons carry. Being small and constructed of stainless steel makes it a perfect hot weather weapon to have with you regardless of how light your clothing is. There are not many firearms that you can carry completely concealed in a swimming suit. Loading it with the new .22 magnum defense rounds gives you five shots that can do a surprising amount of damage to an attacker. I certainly wouldn't want to be hit by it -- and having it beats having nothing.

When it became available, I decided to put the new LaserLyte grip on this gun so that I could extend my effective defensive area. The short barrel makes it pretty ineffective to use rapidly on any target beyond about 7 yards. Adding the LaserLyte allows you to hit point of aim quite a bit further out. The problem I encountered is that while carrying it unholstered in my pocket the laser would bump out of alignment. Not a good thing if you have to depend on it eventually.

So I purchased this Desantis Pocket Holster to protect it. Unfortunately this Desantis holster will not fit around the laser grips. But I also noticed that when the NAA .22 magnum was placed in the holster, the holster was too tight to allow coverage of the trigger. That's not good either. After looking at the holster for a while, I realized that I would have to remove three partial rows of stitching to make it fit. However that would result in the gun sliding around in the holster. After the integrity of the stitching is compromised, it would just be a matter of time before it continued to unwind. Since the holster is designed to stay around the gun as you pull it out of your pocket, it is necessary to make another move to pull the holster from the gun. The Sticky Holster that I use with my Kahr CM9 stays in my pocket when I draw the gun. And the Sticky Holster is about the same size as this Desantis although the Sticky has a much larger space for holding the gun.

Looks like I'll be contacting Sticky Holster instead. I am really happy with their products and I feel very comfortable that they will make a holster to properly fit this combination.

NOTE: 5/11/16 I ordered the proper Sticky Holster after emailing the company and telling them about my problem. They told me to order the holster designed to fit the NAA Pug. It fits perfectly, the trigger is properly covered, and the gun pulls out of the holster leaving the holster in your pocket. Good Job Sticky!
text_fidelity_b: Desantis Nylon Ambidextrous Pocket Holster, Black

This workout works. I had heard about P90x through the infomercials and thought I would give it a try. I have always been in decent shape but I wanted to get "ripped". The first 2 weeks are grueling, you are sore everyday but it feels great. Tony Horton is great, sure some of his lines are corny but he keeps you motivated. By week 4 my arms were the most defined I had ever seen them, by week 6 my abs were coming in pretty nice, and by week 12 WOW. As far as the diet, this was equally important, I did not follow the diet plan to a T but i did do a low carb diet for the first 4 weeks and it helped shred fat. Try this workout, i wish I had done it earlier and will do it again in the future.

2 other points:
(1) Try beachbody on demand, this allows you to pay $40 to stream the workouts for 3.5 months, which is cheaper than the CD's (i used the streaming service).
(2) Don't worry if you gain weight in this program, I went up to 216 after a month because I was burning fat and gaining muscle (i went from 16%-14% fat in month 1). Even so, I looked better at 216 than 212.

We sometimes spend a week or more overlanding (or dispersed camping) and even though we do a lot of hiking and mountain biking, we do miss the gym. Having this set helps to get our strength training exercises in when we do not have access to a gym.

this set is very well made with quality hooks and attachments. I like how each one is marked with its resistance level and they can be combined to increase the resistance as needed. I am a little worried that the laytex won't last as long in the heat of our camper (we live in the dry southwest US) but I guess time will tell. They do carry a great warranty but really at this price as long as the set lasts me a few years, I have no complaints! My last set was not this good of quality and after 5 years one of the handles snapped off during use. I expect this set to last at least that long as the quality seems far superior.
text_fidelity_b: OlarHike Resistance Bands Set, Exercise Bands for Men and Women, Workout Bands with Handles for Working Out, Fitness

text_fidelity_a:
Snowshoes for Adult Unisex,Fully Adjustable Bindings, Lightweight Material, Hard Pack Grip Teeth,Outdoor Aluminum Alloy Material Really like these snowshoes. They are easy to adjust and stay on very well. The bag the shoes came in is first rate as are the poles. My only complaint is that the front binding only ratchets to a point then seem to hang up (it could be the strap end catching on the decking, or perhaps the hard boot material failing to flex)not a huge deal because it is snug enough. Also the pole carrying bag is separate from the shoe bag which means I got to remember to grab both. All in all a nice inexpensive snowshoe. Great for beginners or someone just needing a cheaper option.
12/29/11 UPDATE_ Got to try these out for the first time (not real deep snow- but enough to give them a trial run) These shoes are really nice. I tromped around for about 30 mins and had very few problems (main problem was some ice build up on my heel as I crossed a wet area and the water froze on my boot heel- not a big deal as it can happen with any snowshoe). The bindings did hold well and did not loosen at all. One shoe did seem to be toeing in a bit but that was probably an adjustment issue (it was also a new pair of boots I was trying out.) I'm gonna hopefully get out in some deeper snow next week (yea Lake Effect!)
1/15/12 UPDATE2- Finally got some REAL snow (18+ inches!) and tried these out at my hilly property in the deep woods. AMAZING how well they worked. It was pretty cold (hovering around 16° F in the sun) and the woods were untouched by anything but a few deer and turkeys. These shoes performed great. They never slipped and I did not have to adjust the bindings at all. They do seem to make a bit of noise as far as the bindings creaking (at these temps not to surprising), but nothing broke or loosened. Walked for a little over an hour; over logs, thru brush, uphill, downhill, level, tight twisty area, open fields, deep drifts, and even a snowmobile trail (that crosses the front of our property). These preformed as good as any other shoe. A bonus is I found I really liked the poles- so much so that I gave one to my wife and she really liked using it too. All in all a great purchase- These honestly hover on a 5 star rating- I did have to take away for the pole bag not being attached some way- also the poles are nearly impossible to closeup once they get cold (I think a bit of frost gets into the loosening cam and freezes the pole in place as once they warmed up there were no problems) also there is no place to store the rubber protection cap from the pole. The one show still seemed to toe in a bit- but I only notice it in very shallow snow (less than 6 inches) and the toe binding still only rachets to a certain point and then slips (still not an issue as it is snug enough). Oh and of course the noise factor (not real bad but your not gonna sneak up on anything with these on)
text_fidelity_b: Snowshoes for Adult Unisex,Fully Adjustable Bindings, Lightweight Material, Hard Pack Grip Teeth,Outdoor Aluminum Alloy Material

Now, my nephew can stand and paddle and from watching him on this board, he had no issues while paddling on the lake, meaning it is sturdy and stable.  Me, I have balance issues so instead of standing, I wade out a few feet into the water, get myself seated on the paddleboard and with my legs dangling in the water, I paddle is that seated position.  I had looked at different ways to enjoy the lake - an inner tube you just float and while it's nice to kind of lay back and float, you can't really be proactive in getting yourself here or there in an inner tube.  I really looked at kayaks seriously (and the prices are way out of my price range), but getting in a kayak is a bit more tricky than this paddleboard.  So this is paddleboard, while it is larger and more suited to my nephew, is still a wonderful board that I would have kept had I not found one that fit my frame better.  For taller folks, this is a great board that comes with everything you need to have fun on the water!

text_fidelity_a:
Manduka Prolite Yoga and Pilates Premium Mat 4.7mm Thick / Non-Slip, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly Certified / Made with Ultra Dense Cushioning for Stability and Support The first time I received this product, it was packaged badly so had some unnatural indents that weren't going away. After a few days, I complained to Amazon and they promptly sent me a new one. The new one was in perfect condition, and I was very excited to try it out. I diligently did the salt scrub that they suggest in the instructions, then gave it a try once the mat had dried.

IT WAS SO SLIPPERY. Like insanely slippery. I do not have sweaty hands or feet, and have never had a problem on cheap yoga mats. I am very disappointed that when I finally decided to invest in an expensive yoga mat, I'm met with all of this unnecessary slipping and sliding. It is slippery to the point where it is actually dangerous to use.

I went online and found that this is a very common problem, especially with the prolite mats. I'm now starting on the arduous journey of trying to 'break in' this mat - a process that people say can take months to a year of intense use. Some people online said that they had more success using some soap as well. I have just recently done a very hard scrub using laundry detergent and salt to try to get rid of what they call a "protective film from the factory" that is causing the slipperiness. This process involves finding an outdoor area, spreading your mat flat, sprinkling salt, then scrubbing the mat using the rough side of a sponge for at least 10 minutes with the laundry detergent or dishwashing soap. I will update this post with how many times I have to do this process to make the mat sticky (hopefully not too many times! I might end up giving up and buying a different brand if it takes too much effort)

I really want this yoga mat to work, so I'm going to sacrifice some time and energy into 'breaking it in' just because so many people have told me how their manduka yoga mat has been life changing for their practice. I am still disappointed that it takes this much time and energy though. For how expensive their mat is, the company should be doing the break-in process for us.

Unless you are willing to put in the time and energy to 'break it in' - don't purchase this product. I have heard the Pro (heavier) yoga mat is not as bad as the prolite with it's break-in process, but I haven't bought the pro so I wouldn't know.

Out of the box, this mat is unusable with how slippery it is.
text_fidelity_b: Manduka Prolite Yoga and Pilates Premium Mat 4.7mm Thick / Non-Slip, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly Certified / Made with Ultra Dense Cushioning for Stability and Support

text_fidelity_a: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag First of all, I used to be one of those people who thought trekking poles were for wusses, but as I've gotten a bit older and wiser I have found that they are indispensable for longer hikes. I can hike twice as far with them and they really help with some challenging up and downs. These poles look great and are comfortable to use.  I went on one 10 mile hike when I first used them. I did find that the pole adjustment locks took some getting used to.  You have to turn a knob and then flip the clip to lock it into position. If you tighten the screw too much then there is too much tension and you can't flip the clip, so you have to go back and loosen the screw a bit more and then try again. Once I got the hang of it, it was fairly simple. I would suggest doing it before you leave the house. I'd also suggest leaning hard on each pole to be sure it's locked firmly.  Also, when putting the mud guards on, it helps to screw them on to the threads at the pole bases and then push on firmly. I lost one mudguard (in some really deep mud.) The Foxelli company's customer service is excellent though and they sent a replacement pair out right away!  These come with a nice bag and two sets of tips (one for storage and one for asphalt) and two sets of guards (one for dirt and one for snow.)

text_fidelity_a:
Moultrie Digital Picture Viewer, Black, 2 x 6 x 8.25 I like the viewer pretty well overall. I will tell you what I like first. It's fairly compact. The rubber grip surfaces make it easier to hold. I like that it has uses 4 AAA batteries. Devices with 4 batteries USUALLY have very long battery life, in my experience. It appears that all the covers to the buttons and hatches, etc, are water resistant and maybe waterproof. I like the positive slide on-off "click" of the power button. I love that I can leave one 16gb flashcard internal, and plug in a 2nd flashcard, and then without looking at any of the pictures, transfer everything off the 2nd card to the 1st card (assuming there's room), and then put the 2nd card back into the trail camera. That might be this viewer's best feature--the 2 SD card slots feature. The screen is adequate, altho I feel to really look at the pics, you should look at them on a laptop or desktop computer.

OK, here's what I don't like. I don't like the SD card sticking out of the bottom of the viewer. I would rather it be pressed into the slot and catch with the spring-loaded catch like the internal card slot, and be able to completely close the cover on the SD card. BUT, I realize they may have made it that way so you could take the card out with gloves on, cold fingers, etc. I also don't like how that rubber flap kinda hangs in the breeze when I peel it off to insert a card. I don't like how you can't see all the pics on the screen in a matrix (unless I haven't figured that out yet, and if I'm wrong, I will apologize) and choose from them. I don't like how you have to scroll thru the pics. I also think it takes too long to transfer photos from the trail cam card to the internal card.

I know I'm being nit-picky about some of my dislikes, but I still gave it 4 stars. Oh, also, I paid about $65 (with shipping) not on Amazon Prime, because it wasn't available for Prime when I ordered it, and I noticed today that it was about $51 on Amazon Prime from another vendor. Oh well, it's a decent buy, for sure at $51 and Prime shipping, and an OK buy at $65.
text_fidelity_b: Moultrie Digital Picture Viewer, Black, 2 x 6 x 8.25

Franklin Sports Equipment Bag Multi, One Size If you are looking for an inexpensive solution for storing any size balls, pool toys, sandbox toys and even those light weight self winding hoses, this bag will work. It is made of a hard plastic open weave mesh. We've seen these mesh bags used in smaller sizes for things like plastic soldiers and other plastic toys. It's sturdy enough as long as you use it for light weight and not sharp items.

We have three of these and they are great on a hook in the garage for keeping things off the floor and organized. We use one for our variety of basketballs, soccer balls and baseballs. What is great, is when these balls get dirty, we do a quick hose off and just throw them in the mesh bag. They air dry perfect when hanging.

We also keep our self winding hoses in the bag- again the light weight hoses dry perfect hanging in the bag. And last we found this bag perfect for pool and sandbox toys. A quick hose off and they air dry in the bag. With three bags, we have eliminated ball, hose and toy clutter and it's so convenient to just hose and bag these items to air dry. As long as the items are light weight and not sharp, I can see the bag lasting even with it's inexpensive construction.

text_fidelity_a:
Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick I've previously owned a Klymit V without the "Luxe," but a piece of the one valve it had broke off in short order. This Klymit V Luxe has valves which *appear* to me to have fewer fiddly parts, and there are two of them--more on why that's good in a moment!

First off, these pads have a smart design. Although there is no railing per say, the Vs help to keep you on them which is good news if you do not stay in one place on a bed. The material keeps the air inside from feeling cold (and presumably from drinking in too much of the earth's cold).

The primary use I gave my original V was as a buffer between me and an extremely ill-suited new mattress while I desperately shopped for solutions. And although I've been a backpacker in the past, sadly, my primary intended use for the Static V Luxe is to act as a buffering layer when I need to sleep on other people's mattresses. I have considerable back health issues, and this padding is incredibly helpful for when I cannot be on my own mattress. I purchased this size this time because the original V is so much smaller than a twin bed that it was downright silly trying to use it for my purpose. Also I use a body pillow and change positions a lot. This will clearly be nicer for managing nights out of my own bed.

Now I saw someone complaining about the two valves because they are confusing. This person has probably never experienced the downsides of only having one valve for letting air out of a mattress. Sure, you need to be certain that the valve you are not blowing into is closed so that the mattress can properly inflate, but oh, my word, it is soooooo much easier to get the air out of this mattress pad! I could almost never get my original V small enough to properly stick into its dry sack. But this larger V luxe easily packs up smaller than I could get the original V to go. Ok, so maybe "easy" is relative. You do need to open both valves, roll it down from bottom to top, open it up again, fold a few times, and roll once more to get it maximally small. But it actually works and stuffs in the drysack.

I hope if you're reading this that you have more adventurous uses afoot, but I do recommend this Static V Luxe and wish I'd had one back when I was a backpacker!
text_fidelity_b: Klymit Insulated Static V Luxe Inflatable Sleeping Pad for Camping, Lightweight Hiking and Backpacking Air Bed For Cold Weather, 3 Inch Thick

text_fidelity_a:
SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish I purchased this knife as a semi-impulse buy. I had been looking for a new edc for a couple months, however I was skeptic to stray away from my kershaw of 5 years.

After my initial purchase I read many mixed reviews, and after a month of carrying here are my thoughts.

PROS:
1) The low profile pocket clip doesn't scratch the crap out of my car paint as my kershaw did.
2) The metal is not as good as my kershaw, but it is VERY VERY close.
3) A ceramic hone works best after sharpening.
4) You can get this thing RAZOR sharp, but it dulls after a moderate amount of use.
5) It is SUPER light, and very fast.
6) Initially the opening mechanism is weird getting used to. However once you do, it is actually very easy to use.
7) The short blade does NOT impede its performance as I originally thought. You can think the belly of the knife for this, it adds a nice additional cutting surface.
8) The anodized aluminum is fairly slip resistant.
9) The thumb studs protrude enough for you to get a good open on it.
10) It is very sleek looking and the POP is an attention getter.
11) It is pretty ergonomic and it fits in the hand pretty well.

CONS:
1) It is difficult getting adjusted to the opening mechanism.
2) The "safety" makes me feel like this thing will jump open in my pocket if I don't have it turned on.... even though it probably wont.
3) I don't care for lock back knives as it impedes one handed use. I now can use it one handed though which took some practice.
4) The metal is odd, things you think would dull it won't.... but the things you don't think would will.. I.E. it cuts through weed eater string like a beast but a couple pieces of thin cardboard has this blade spent.
5) Tape and other adhesives stick to this blade BAD... My kershaw had a Teflon coating. Something I wished this one had.
6) the top of the pocket clip sticks up about 3/16 of an inch from the knife.... it is just odd to me. It doesn't really affect the functionality however.

Even though I questioned my purchase at first, I am very happy with my purchase. For this price you get a PERFECT edc knife. Just make sure that you have at least an 800-1200 grit diamond stone and a ceramic hone for quick sharpening.
text_fidelity_b: SOG Specialty Knives & Tools BBA99-CP Blink Knife with Straight Edge Assisted Folding 2.25-Inch AUS-8 Steel Blade and Aluminum Handle, Satin Finish

text_fidelity_a:
Burley Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer 2016 UPDATE: Every replacement tire for this trailer (12.5 inch tire) is total junk, except one: the [[ASIN:B00I3U8MSG Schwalbe HS158 Wheelchair Tire - Wire Bead (Grey - 12 1/2 x 2 1/4)]]. Trust me, I tried them all by now.
UPDATE:
After three years I decided to change the tires on this trailer. By luck I discovered that there exist 12.5 in scooter tires and pocket bike tires in widths of 2.5 and 2.75 inches. I opted for a pair of 2.75 knobby pocket bike tires in the hope that the added width would prevent some of tip overs I describe below. HUGE DIFFERENCE! I could still make this trailer tip with little difficulty but it is far more stable with the improved tires. So if you're considering this trailer be prepared to change the stock tires immediately (<$20x2 with free shipping if you shop carefully). You'll still want to run with low tire pressure but not nearly as low as with the stock tires. If you opt not to change the tires, read on so you know what to expect and read the comments, too.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
For what it is (the materials) this trailer seems over-priced. It sometimes tips over (often enough) traversing street and sidewalk surfaces via a handicap ramp and driveways (and vice versa). If and when it tips over the trailer doesn't take the bike (and you) with it, but if you are traversing from sidewalk to street, it tips in the middle of the intersection. Not good.

The trailer tires call for 35 PSI Max and if those tires are fully inflated with an empty load, this trailer will bounce all over creation at any larger imperfections in the riding surface and is at serious risk of tipping over.

The tilted, upward-leaning design approach (like a hand truck) is a good one because the footprint is small, it is easy to maneuver when un-hitched and one need not bend far over to access the trailer and its contents. The footprint is small enough so I sometimes take it on a transit bus without concern. But I believe the upward design, hitching to the seat post rather than the rear-wheel axle, as with most trailers, is the source of the stability problems.

The strapping system (2 are included) is just okay. You can do just as well or better with quality bungies. I bought some of the bags that Burley dedicates to this trailer but returned them. I now just cinch a plastic clothes hamper to the trailer with bungies and the hamper holds a ton.

A few things can be done to minimize the bouncing and tipping:

1. when unloaded, reduce the trailer tire pressure to 10 PSI or lower. The problem with this is if you go from empty to a moderate or full load in the same trip, you'll need to inflate the tires mid-trip, closer to max PSI to accommodate the additional load.

2. traverse driveways and handicap ramps completely perpendicular so that you don't catch a trailer tire on the ramp's raised shoulders.

3. slow down (a lot) in anticipation of any significant road imperfection for when 1 and 2 are difficult or impossible.

After close to two years I still use this trailer almost daily for shopping but I've learned to slow way down when traversing from sidewalk to street and keep my tire pressure to 10PSI or less when unloaded or with a light-to-moderate load to prevent tipping. Even with the PSI under 10, there are particular handicap ramps that I traverse frequently over which, if I don't slow down significantly, the trailer will tip over. Every time. No exaggeration.

I'm not completely sorry I own this trailer; it has a lot going for it: small footprint, carry-on size for air travel, etc, but I believe it needs some type of suspension to prevent tipping to make it a better value at $299.
text_fidelity_b: Burley Travoy, Compact Folding Cargo Bike Trailer

My wife and I are thrilled to have it! A few months ago my wife several broke her foot and has been off it. As the doctor lets her get back on it - and encourages slow exercise to help her rebuild leg muscles, I wanted to find something for her to do that would get her up, but not over do it. Bocce Ball can be played over a very large area - we controlled it by just going back and forth - but it got us outside, into the sun, and moving. She could take breaks and we had a blast! I grabbed the regulation set - figuring it was best overall for weight and size. I have never played before and she hadn’t played since she was a teen. We had to use the instructions, but it was pretty easy to learn. And our local park was the perfect place.

1. It comes in a great bag - the full set fits well into the bag, which is well designed and built. It’s a strong material, looks great - with the logo - and the zipper is strong. This is a pretty heavy set of balls and this bag holds up well. It looks great out there too.
2. There are three nets in the bag, each holding 3 balls - or two balls and the small ball and measuring string.
3. There is a set of instructions - my wife read it and talked me through it. It’s been easy to learn and play.
4. The balls for this set weigh a great amount - it wasn’t long before we had a feel for them and able to play well - a difference between long play or short.
5. The balls can take it. In this state the ground is a bit hard and the grass isn’t the best, and we were throwing them a good distance. After 3 games over 2 days they still look perfect. I’m not saying we beat them up, but we put them through playing - these are really nice. They look nice, hold nice, have a great balance. I really have no game of reference, but this is a great set.

I literally played for the first time this weekend and I loved it! This was a great game for my wife and I - not just as she recovers from her foot injury, but in general. We have every intention of getting many years out of this set - playing often. We took it easy because of her recovery, but we know we’ll be able to cover a lot of ground in the future (grass, sand, whatever). It is a fun game with a need for some talent - but yet something most nay member of the family can play. Our regulation set is fairly heavy - we are guessing not as heavy as tournament - so something to consider if playing with kids. But we have had a lot of fun, shared a lot of laughs, and enjoyed spending the time playing. We are thrilled with this JAPER BEES Bocce Ball Set and look forward to many more years playing.

I would not describe these as being soft or cozy. These are targeted at being travel blankets that should stay cleaner and drier for longer. A negative to this material is that it blocks moisture from escaping, so you can end up sweaty, especially if you are sleeping in a car without any airflow. This stores nicely in a case that can be used as a pillow. I got both the down and down alternative blankets. The down alternative blanket is thinner due to less filler material used. Both are sufficiently warm. The down alternative version should be more resistant to accumulating allergens. The down version offers more padding if you are lying down on this. Neither version offers significant padding if you are lying down on these as the filler is not dense enough to support body weight. The 45 x 80 size is enough to cover one adult unless you are obese. I washed both in a washing machine, and they came out fine.

My sleeping bag is made out of the same material on one side, and has more comfortable cotton on the inner side, with significantly more filling. It can completely unzip to use as a blanket. Depending on the scenario, a sleeping bag can be more versatile, although it takes up more room and is not designed to be used alternatively as a pillow.

I chose this particular one because I wanted springs rather than the bungee type cords that could wear out faster  It does make a little spring noise but if you have music going you’re not going to notice it at all. The jump area was larger than expected and very nice. I am getting serious workouts on this thing with very limited movements on my part.  Putting it together was super simple it came in a taco shape and you just opened it up and then lifted the legs up and they went into place. The instructions did note to be careful when I unfolding which I did not read and I did smash my finger LOL my instructions showed a different stability bar that had bolts to hold it in.  I don’t know if that was for an older model or what but it makes me kind a wish that the handle did fasten with bolts.  Don’t be scared of my negativity though as far as the handle goes I am only reviewing this on how I feel about it for my own personal use and like I said I do have very restricted mobility and balance.  I would recommend this to others. You can get a serious workout in 20 to 30 minutes. For those of you wondering about the size; if you are familiar with the round Costco dog beds it’s about the same size as that.

text_fidelity_a:
Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs I’ll be honest, I’d never heard about exercise plate machines until I saw this one. I looked it up and according to the articles I was reading, this is an under used exercise machine type and actually does help loose weight. So I decided to grab this LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine and try it. I come away surprised, but happy - it does help me. My wife and I have been active in living a healthier lifestyle and approach with a variety of activities, from kickboxing and walking to weights to... well, this thing. My wife is still sidelined from her severely broken foot, so she has not tried it yet, but I have and I’m blown away by how it works.

The machine arrives in a box that is easy to remove from - all the parts are fit correctly and easy to get out. It is slightly heavy - nothing one can’t move, but it has some weight to it. I’m not sure the actual size, but we can’t fit it under our bed, so we’re still working on where to keep it - but that’s not an issue. There are instructions - I would suggest also doing a little research. I learned a few things from articles I was reading. There are also resistance bands and for your arms resistance ropes as well. The instructions are well done and offer ideas for working out as well.

The unit has a remote so you don’t have to get off or bend down to alter things. I have used it every time - I will increase or decrease the various options while still on it. This comes in handy for severity of the vibration as it is intense and I’ll inch it up or down during the workout. I have not gone very high - I want to say around 15 - and appreciate being able to try things or adjust as I need.

ONE CON: The power cord is short. I have to use it primarily in our bedroom where my wife is currently working from bed, so that limits when I can use it. If it were at least another 2 - 3 feet long it would be perfect. I’m going to move some things around and try to make it work in the living room, but if not... anyways, if they changed that this would be a perfect unit.

I really love the workout. It is... (not) easy. I mean you’re standing on this vibrating plate and you do feel it. The level, the time, going up and down, the truth is, your body works to stay there. I’ve only stood on it and done planks, and both were workouts. I got off sweating. I’ll say, standing on it is less of a vibration to my head than the plank - I can’t go as long or as high at a single time because in the plank position I feel like my head will vibrate off. But I can feel my core working.

I like this unit so much that when I saw a foot massager from the same company I grabbed it. While you can use this as a foot vibrator, I thought to help my wife heal - when cleared by the doctor - she might be able to use that foot massager to advance her healing - but again, I grabbed that because of this company - I was that impressed.

Overall the LifePro Waver Mini Press Vibration Plate Exercise Machine is a great workout tool and we are happy to have it. I feel like it has added to my workout and will aide me in getting into the shape I’m working towards and my goals.
text_fidelity_b: Lifepro Waver Mini Vibration Plate - Whole Body Vibration Platform Exercise Machine - Home & Travel Workout Equipment for Weight Loss, Toning & Wellness - Max User Weight 260lbs

text_fidelity_a:
Topeak Adjustable Modula Cage EX Modified Shape Bicycle Waterbottle Cage Updated 6/18/14 - As predicted the plastic did break. While riding on a slightly bumpy road with a half filled bottle in the cage, the two plastic areas at the mount points simply gave way. The fix is fairly simple but may require a quick trip to a hardware store. Using rubber washers against the plastic and metal washers against the frame (mount points) and bolt heads, the cage is now [probably] better than new. I doubt it will break again, as the new mounting method distributes weight/load more evenly across the plastic, and the rubber washers offer a bit of shock-resistance. Hopefully the manufacturer will read this, having likely heard similar reports from other customers, and fix the issue - if not done already. I still like the design and flexibility.

Original Review: The only problem here is the plastic to metal nut that tightens down to hold the sliding cage in place. I do not see that lasting for a long time. But with a trip to the hardware store I was able to get all metal parts, with washers to protect the plastic cage, hoping to avoids cracks and snaps down the road. If you only use one size container, thus unlikely to move it around, the this should work just fine.
The great thing is that this does hold nearly any bottle within the size range in place, without issue. Even when mountain biking I had no problems with the 12oz Poland Springs bottle that was in there.
text_fidelity_b: Topeak Adjustable Modula Cage EX Modified Shape Bicycle Waterbottle Cage

text_fidelity_a: VX-Power Seated Elliptical Bike - Electric Under Desk Mini Elliptical Machine, Feet Massager, Compact Pedal Exerciser for Seniors, Home Office Leg Workout Exercise Equipment w/Remote & LCD Display Okay, I think this elliptical is a decent, portable version, especially for those without room for a full size machine (would love one, but really could not fit one in my house!).  The problem I have had with it is the roller massagers.  Don't get me wrong, I love a good foot massage...but rollers don't work for me and my sensitive soles.  If they were tiny, like no larger than a BB pellet, that might work, but these feel honkin' BIG against the soles of my feet and they HURT.  Plus, they are still right there in the pedal even when you aren't getting a message.  I have dry eye syndrome and have a kind of space age-looking eye cover that has similar massager balls that goes around and "squeeze" my eyeballs and these don't bother me.  I just can't handle a lot of things against the soles of my feet - rocks felt through my shoes nearly bring me to tears, that's how bad it is with my feet.  So...I did my best to work around the issue with thickly padded pieces that fit over the pedal area to nullify the feeling of the massage balls against my skin and that's working, but I shouldn't have to do that.  I do enjoy using the machine - I am older and need the exercise and this is good for getting in steps even when the weather is bad and I can't just walk in pouring rain, 60 MPH winds or really cold weather.  Just wish the massager part was made differently.  Heck, I have a "foot massager" that is like a giant Tens unit pad that transmits a small shock of electricity to the skin and deeper, to the muscle tissue.  That actually gives me a really decent "massage" that soothes and calms my aching feet if I've been walking/standing too long.  I mention this as a possible suggestion for a different type of massage that won't require large rollers!  Maybe if you don't suffer from sensitive feet this machine will work great for you just as it is.
text_fidelity_b: VX-Power Seated Elliptical Bike - Electric Under Desk Mini Elliptical Machine, Feet Massager, Compact Pedal Exerciser for Seniors, Home Office Leg Workout Exercise Equipment w/Remote & LCD Display

This is in case you are lost or feel for your safety.". Far too often established campgrounds are most with the sounds of people's generators, children, animals, music, etc. A scream for help would be as useless as a whisper. A whistle has the ability to be heard over long distances and other man-made and natural noises.

Three blasts from a whistle is the same as an SOS. People, especially emergency and first responders are trained to respond to SOS whistles. These are not toys.

text_fidelity_a:
Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch Here I am again, this time I'm looking for the best pouch possible for a very specific carry option. I've wanted something to carry one of my home made mini EDC kits, plus a few other items. I've found some really nice models, but they were usually too big or too small. Some were a great size for my needs, but were cost prohibitive.

Alas, I found a Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch on Amazon for about $14. I had narrowed it down to this item over a Condor Gadget MOLLE Pouch. The prices were nearly identical, so I went over both items with a discerning eye. The Monstrum was about a half-inch smaller, so it was a close call.

I believe some Monstrum products mimic their higher priced competition, yet still make a great value. There may be subtle differences here and there, but there were no major must-haves. I rarely go for the high end products when I find one that is similar for a lower price and good reviews. A quick note on reviews? Take them ALL with a grain of salt.

The Monstrum pouch appears to be very well made. The stitching appears sturdy and I only found one loose thread, which I burned down in about 3 seconds. It was a small detail, but it lent itself to the overall quality. The zippers, zipper pulls, and Velcro patches are also solid.

Features on the pouch were way more than I expected and what I saw online. As I looked it over, right after opening the Amazon box, I knew I had hit a homerun. From the front, there is a hard pouch cover with a zippered pocket. On the underside of that cover is a heavy duty patch of Velcro that connects to the front, expandable, pocket. On either side of that pocket are elastic loops that can be adjusted to hold the pocket tightly closed. In this front area, you have it subdivided into different sections. Behind this front area, you have the main pocket. It has 3 subdivisions and they held everything I wanted with a tiny bit of room left. This main pocket has two zippers w/pulls. On the back of the pouch, there are two MOLLE snap straps, which are useful to wear on a belt, if you know how to weave them correctly.

One of the main things that I liked was the expandable front pocket. It really protrudes as you add more stuff, so those adjustable elastic straps help it stay secure. It more than serves its purpose.

Pros:
Cost @ $14
Strong & sturdy
Perfect size for a mini-EDC kit and other small items
Multiple carry options

Cons:
It looks pregnant with all the stuff I put in there, so that's a bit odd.
(As was that statement).

Final verdict? Take a close look for yourself on the Monstrum or Amazon websites and see for yourself. If you have a couple of handfuls of small-ish gear you want to keep in its own pouch, this may work out perfect for you too.
text_fidelity_b: Monstrum Tactical MOLLE Utility Pouch

text_fidelity_a:
Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology I purchased the Igloo BMX Cooler to replace an Ozark Trail 25qt rotomolded cooler that I purchased from Wal-Mart before an impromptu camping trip. I was very disappointed with the OT cooler, it claimed to hold ice for 4.5 days but on day two of my trip over half the ice was melted. I had a family member coming out to visit and camp with me so I decided to order the 52qt version of the Igloo BMX. It was actually cheaper than the Wal-Mart cooler and twice the size.

We filled the Igloo up on a Sunday afternoon packed pretty full with food, beer and water. We were planning on a 3-day trip. I saved as much ice as I could at home and we bought one more bag on the way out of town. Day 1 after over 24 hours I opened the drain and only a tiny bit of water came out. Already much better performance. On Tuesday we moved campsites and got gas and added another bag of ice since we bought more food to replenish. Day 3 on Wednesday a fair amount of water drained from the cooler but it still had plenty of ice and was plenty cold. I had put 8 frozen water bottles inside and they were all frozen still.

I went to empty the cooler on Day 4, a full ~96 hours of use and there was still a lot of ice left in it. I have no doubt that you could make this last 5 days or even longer if you keep adding fresh ice every couple of days. If we didn't add the second bag, most of it would have probably melted by day 3/4.

At the time of this review I purchased the red/black 52qt cooler for $77. I'm impressed enough with it that I decided to order a 25qt one was well for solo trips and returned my Ozark Trail cooler. I will add another review or update this one after I use the 25qt cooler. But $140 for a nice rotomolded 52qt and 25qt cooler is less than half the price of ONE comparable Yeti. So glad I didn't buy into the hype.
text_fidelity_b: Igloo BMX 52 Quart Cooler with Cool Riser Technology

Consumers are assured that products bearing the SEI label have been manufactured to meet the level of quality and performance of the most current comprehensive standards existing for the product. Having a large number of balls makes it easy for coaches to quickly run drills without having to stop and wait on equipment.
